Title: Unredacted credentials leaked via /api/identity rawConfig
Description: app/api/identity/route.ts read openclaw.json verbatim via fs.readFileSync and returned it as rawConfig in the JSON response with no redaction, exposing gateway auth token and Telegram botToken to any client hitting the endpoint or viewing /identity page source.
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Ensure openclaw.json contains a credential field (e.g. gateway.auth.token, channels.telegram.botToken)
2. curl http://localhost:3333/api/identity
3. Inspect rawConfig, openclawConfig, and providers fields in response
Expected Result: Credential values redacted/masked in all API response fields
Actual Result: Full raw token values (e.g. gateway.auth.token, telegram botToken) returned in plaintext in rawConfig and openclawConfig
Environment:
OS: Windows 11
Next.js 16.1.6
Node.js (local dev, npm run dev)
Resolution: Added redactSecrets()/redactJsonString() to lib/sanitize.ts (masks string values on keys matching /token|key|secret|password|credential|auth/i, keeping last 4 chars). Applied to openclawConfig, providers, and rawConfig in app/api/identity/route.ts. Verified via curl: token and botToken now return as ****b8b2 / ****FEhA.

Title: Critical/high severity dependency vulnerabilities (simple-git RCE
Steps to Reproduce: npm audit reported 20 vulnerabilities (1 critical 10 high 8 moderate 1 low). Critical: simple-git <=3.35.2 vulnerable to RCE via blockUnsafeOperationsPlugin bypass (GHSA-r275-fr43-pm7q), direct dependency used in lib/git/repo.ts. High: next 16.1.6 had 11 high-severity advisories including middleware/proxy bypass, SSRF via WebSocket upgrades, DoS via Server Components and Cache Components, direct dependency.
Expected Result:
1. cd project root
2. npm audit --json
3. Inspect vulnerabilities.simple-git and vulnerabilities.next entries
Actual Result: No critical or high severity vulnerabilities in direct or transitive dependencies
Environment: 1 critical (simple-git RCE) + 10 high (next.js CVEs, vite, undici, hono, etc.) present
Resolved Date: Ran npm audit fix (cleared most transitive high/critical). Ran npm audit fix --force to pull next@16.2.10 (non-major, fixes 11 high-severity CVEs). Manually upgraded simple-git to ^3.36.0 (patched RCE). Remaining: 2 moderate (postcss, nested inside next's own deps) left unresolved -- fixing requires downgrading next to 9.3.3 (breaking), not worth the regression. Verified app boots clean on next 16.2.10 via dev server, spot-checked /api/crons returns 200.
